correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the upper count by placing a support of size s at the s cheapest exponents, multiplying 1+floor(n/2^(j+1)) over those exponents, then allowing at most 2^(k+1) supports. This gives log_2 b_{<=t} <= tk-t^2/2+O(k) for admissible t. The matching lower bound fixes consecutive exponents 0 through s-1, draws the multiplicity parameters at j>=1 from independent boxes of total cost <=n/4, and completes the sum at j=0. Oddness of n and of the baseline 2^s-1 gives an integer nonnegative parameter at j=0, and different boxed choices give different partitions. The log volume is sk-s^2/2+O(k log(k+2)) with the error uniform in the allowed s; use s=t for fixed epsilon and s=k-O(log k) for the total. Subtraction yields exactly the two-sided tail exponent with its stated error. The support weight 2^(J-1) then gives the claimed upper bound 2^k and lower bound 2^t(1-o(1)) for the mean on odd indices only. Independently checked exact support histograms for 1<=n<=255 by direct odd-multiplicity recursion against H(2m)=H(m) and H(2m+1)=H(2m-1)+zH(m), with H(0)=1 and H(1)=z. The finite replay is python3 /tmp/opencode/frozen_independent_checks.py (line beginning 3:).
residual_risks: The finite check tests histograms, not any asymptotic limit. Epsilon is fixed for the tail assertion. No all-integer separation or multiplicative equivalent follows.

value.rationale: The two-sided law measures how rarely a uniformly chosen odd-multiplicity partition uses a given small fraction of the available sizes. It goes beyond proving concentration near full logarithmic support, and reveals the statistic connecting two established self-similar sequences. This is a meaningful distributional result even after crediting the existing ratio and one-sided bound.
residual_risks: Only logarithmic-scale rare-event estimates are proved. Near-typical fluctuations, a local limit, and a sharp ratio equivalent are not established.
